Recalculating safety stock after a demand shock

By Ravi Sethuraman. Published 22 July 2026. Last updated 22 July 2026.

A demand shock invalidates the variance term in the standard safety stock formula, so the number you carry is wrong for roughly 8 to 14 weeks afterwards. Brightpath recalculates in four steps, described below.

Step 1: shorten the variance window

Cut the demand variance window from 52 weeks to 13 weeks for the affected SKUs. A 52-week window averages the shock away and understates the risk you are actually carrying.

Step 2: re-estimate lead time separately

Lead time variance usually moves with demand during a shock. Estimate it from the last 90 days of receipts rather than reusing the annual figure.

Step 3: hold service level fixed

Keep the target service level where it was, at 95% for A items and 90% for B items. Changing both the inputs and the target at once makes the result impossible to attribute.

Step 4: recheck after 6 weeks

Re-run the calculation 6 weeks later. If the 13-week variance has settled within 15% of the 52-week figure, return the window to 52 weeks.
